name: Maxwell-V1.0-Flash
context_scaling: native to 262144 (card's configured sequence length, and the trained length). config.json max_position_embeddings 524288 with rope_theta 20000000 and no rope_scaling key, so 512K is the RoPE-supported ceiling but not a trained or claimed length
attention_variant: block-sparse GQA (MBSA): dense attention over a 16K query-position prefix plus 8 local + 8 prefix + up to 16 indexer-selected remote 128-token blocks per KV group, bounded at 4096 tokens of main attention per KV group; full-history KV cache is still kept
notes: ADDED 2026-11-17 from the HF createdAt feed (repo 2026-10-13, 171k downloads, 79 likes - low-traffic launch, not a trending spike). A 35B-total / 3B-active text-only MoE that PASSES THE HARDWARE GATE as an expert-offload target: only 12 of 256 routed experts fire per token, so decode traffic is a small slice of the ~74 GB BF16 checkpoint and the experts can live in system RAM. PARAMS: HF safetensors total 36,810,559,422 BF16, so params_b 36.811 is the measured count, not the card's nameplate. active_params_b 3.0 is the card's own 35B/3B 'both excluding embeddings' figure - not derived here. ARITHMETIC: params_b x 0.5 GiB = 18.4 GiB of weights at 4-bit, so the gate (<=128) passes with wide margin; flops_per_token_active = 2 x 3.0e9 = 6.0e9 is the schema one-pass approximation. GEOMETRY from config.json fetched 2026-11-17: hidden 2048, 45 layers, 32 query heads, 4 kv heads, head_dim 128 (gqa_ratio 8); 256 experts, 12 per token, moe_intermediate_size 512, shared_expert_intermediate_size 1024; mlp_only_layers [0,1,2] so 3 layers are dense FFN and 42 are MoE. KV (bf16): 45 x 4 kv heads x 128 x 2 (K+V) x 2 bytes = 92,160 B/token. The block-sparse attention BOUNDS compute, not storage - the card says the full-history KV cache stays available, so all 45 layers are counted. EXTRA ARCHITECTURE the schema has no field for: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (enable_hyper_connections true, num_residual_streams 4), a sigmoid router with expert bias, and mtp_num_layers 1. WHY IT EARNED A RECORD - it beats the catalog's best 30-40B / <=6B-active figure on tests measured on the same benchmark, all as VENDOR CLAIMS with no third-party reproduction: LiveCodeBench v6 pass@1 85.66 vs the class's KRAFTON Raon-1 mini preview 81.6; AIME 2025 mean@8 96.25 vs Rio-2.5-Open 93.33 (its pass@8 is a saturated 100.00); MMLU-Pro 85.46 vs Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 85.3 (a 0.16 gap - treat as a tie); MMMLU 92.0 vs Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 85.2; Tau3-Bench 67.37 vs Xing4.0-29B-A4B 64.63. EVERY ONE IS A VENDOR-ONLY COMPARISON and the class-best values are themselves vendor claims from other cards, so the wins are same-test, not same-harness. WHAT IT LOSES, printed on its own card: Terminal-Bench 2.1 58.65 to Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B 67.8; HLE (128K) 24.79 to Axion 1.0-35B 52.8; BrowseComp 76.30 to Sage-A1.5 82.8; DeepSearchQA 83.30 to XYZ-Aquila-mini 89.5; WideSearch 74.40 to XYZ-Aquila-mini 80.8; IFBench 64.80 to Recursive Flint 89.2; IFEval 93.00 to LFM2.5-24B-A2B 96.75. So the win is math (AIME/HMMT/IMO-AnswerBench: mathematical average mean@8 92.61, the best mean@8 in the class) and live code, not agentic terminal work or scale-dependent knowledge. PROSE NUMBERS on the card that are NOT benchmark rows and are not recorded here: MBSA kernel 6.7x faster than dense GQA at 256K, ~26T training tokens, Muon optimizer, 66x storage claim does not appear here (that is MemT).
